Interpret a fitted STABL selection

Source: R/interpretation.R
stabl_interpret.Rd

Builds a canonical feature-evidence table for a fitted stabl_fit() or stabl() object without re-running STABL. For each feature the table records the stability score, the selection flag, a conditional signed effect from a separately fitted downstream model, a reproducible correlation/redundancy group, and a seeded permutation importance.

Usage

stabl_interpret(
  object,
  x,
  y,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial"),
  assessment = FALSE,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman"),
  cor_threshold = 0.7,
  n_repeats = 20L,
  loss = NULL,
  random_state = NULL,
  event_class = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted "stabl_fit" or "stabl" object.

x

Feature matrix (samples × features) with row and column names. Must contain every selected feature; extra columns are ignored.

y

Outcome aligned to the rows of x (named vector or factor).

family

"gaussian" or "binomial"; the downstream effect model.

assessment

Logical; set TRUE only when x/y are genuinely held out from the fitting procedure. Changes the evaluation_scope label, nothing else.

cor_method

"pearson" or "spearman".

cor_threshold

Numeric in [0, 1]; |correlation| at which two features join one redundancy group.

n_repeats

Number of permutation repeats for importance.

loss

Loss for permutation importance: "squared_error" (gaussian), "brier" or "log_loss" (binomial).

random_state

Seed for permutation importance.

event_class

For binomial, the level treated as the event; defaults to the second level of the outcome factor.

...

Reserved for future use.

Value

An object of class "stabl_interpretation": a list with evidence (the canonical data.frame), effects_model (the downstream fit), correlation (method, threshold, groups), importance (per-repeat matrix and settings), event_class, family, and provenance (call, seed, scopes). Missing or unestimable entries are explicit NA with a reason column.

Details

Evidence labels. All effects and importances are computed on the data supplied as x/y. When that data is the fitting data, every row is labelled post_selection_descriptive (effects) and apparent (importance): the same samples informed both selection and the downstream fit, so the quantities are optimistic and carry no inferential meaning. Supplying genuinely held-out x/y relabels the importance scope, but the caller is responsible for that data being untouched by fitting — this function cannot verify it.

What each column is. stability is the max-over-lambda selection frequency from get_importances(); it is not a coefficient magnitude or a prediction importance. coefficient / standardized_effect / effect_direction come from a downstream stats::glm() fit on the selected features only and are conditional, descriptive associations. correlation_group is a reproducible high-|correlation| cluster; it is increase in loss when the feature is permuted (positive = helpful); negative values are retained.

Examples

set.seed(1L)
x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 8), 60, 8,
            dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:60), paste0("f", 1:8)))
y <- setNames(0.8 * x[, "f1"] + rnorm(60), rownames(x))
fit <- stabl_fit(x, y,
                 lambda_grid = data.frame(lambda = c(0.3, 0.1, 0.05)),
                 n_bootstraps = 10L, artificial_type = "random_permutation",
                 random_state = 1L)
insight <- stabl_interpret(fit, x, y, family = "gaussian", n_repeats = 3L)
summary(insight)
#>   feature selected stability selection_threshold coefficient
#> 1      f1     TRUE       1.0                 0.8   0.6703844
#> 2      f2     TRUE       1.0                 0.8  -0.2830241
#> 3      f6     TRUE       0.9                 0.8   0.2003799
#>   standardized_effect effect_direction  effect_measure correlation_group
#> 1           0.5732918         positive mean_difference                 1
#> 2          -0.2587687         negative mean_difference                 2
#> 3           0.1986708         positive mean_difference                 3
#>   permutation_importance importance_sd importance_n_repeats
#> 1              0.6607421    0.21953776                    3
#> 2              0.1551685    0.10762615                    3
#> 3              0.1204917    0.03422392                    3
#>                evidence_type evaluation_scope n_observations         model_id
#> 1 post_selection_descriptive     fitting_data             60 downstream_refit
#> 2 post_selection_descriptive     fitting_data             60 downstream_refit
#> 3 post_selection_descriptive     fitting_data             60 downstream_refit
#>   na_reason
#> 1      <NA>
#> 2      <NA>
#> 3      <NA>
